full: 'Abdur Rahman bin Khalid ibn al-Walid b. al-Mughirah b. 'Abdullah b. 'Umar b. Makhzum b. Yaqazah
full_name_ar: عبد الرحمن بن خالد بن الوليد المخزومي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The Wikipedia article gives him as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid of Banu Makhzum, son of the general Khalid ibn al-Walid, born c. 616 and died 666. He was governor of Homs under the caliphs 'Uthman and Mu'awiya, fought at Siffin against 'Ali, and led winter campaigns against the Byzantines in 664-666. He is said to have been poisoned by Mu'awiya's Christian physician Ibn Uthal because of rivalry over the succession, and is buried in Homs. The article cites modern scholarship (Blankinship, Gibb, Hinds, Hawting, Morony).
research_evidence: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid (Arabic: عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَن بْنِ خَالِد بْنِ الْوَلِيد; 616–666) was the governor of Homs

He lived long, reportedly 115 years, lost his sight in the time of 'Uthman, and died in Medina in 54 AH / 674 CE.

bio: Fayruz al-Daylami was a Persian (Daylamite) companion of the Prophet, descended from the Persians whom Khosrow I had sent to Yemen. He converted to Islam around 631 CE, and the Prophet ordered him to divorce one of his two wives because they were sisters, a report preserved in Sunan Abu Dawud and Sunan Ibn Majah. He killed the false prophet al-Aswad al-Ansi in 632 CE and may afterwards have governed Sanaa. The page cites al-Tabari's History and the TDV Encyclopedia of Islam; his death is placed either in Uthman's caliphate or in 673 CE under Mu'awiya, so no single year is recorded.

bio: Entry 5844 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal: Mikhmar ibn Mu'awiya, also identified as Hakim ibn Mu'awiya al-Numayri, a companion of the Prophet. He narrated from the Prophet the hadith on there being no ill omen, and that good fortune may lie in three things: a woman, a horse and a house. His nephew Hakim ibn Mu'awiya (or Mu'awiya ibn Hakim) narrated from him, and al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah recorded his hadith. No death year is given.

bio: Entry 6598 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal (continued on the following page): Hulb al-Ta'i, father of Qabisa ibn Hulb. It is said Hulb was a nickname and that his name was Yazid ibn 'Adi ibn Qunafa ibn 'Adi ibn 'Abd Shams ibn 'Adi ibn Akhzam of Tayy. He narrated from the Prophet and his son Qabisa ibn Hulb narrated from him; Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith. The entry says he came to the Prophet bald, the Prophet wiped his head and his hair grew, and that he settled in Kufa; fuller details are given under his son Qabisa. No death year is given.

bio: Entry 7372 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal (kunya section): Abu Zuhayr al-Thaqafi, father of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, a companion of the Prophet. bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal, Book of Kunyas (entry 7578, pages 18322-18323), gives Abu Qays, mawla of Amr ibn al-As, whose name according to Abu Sa'id ibn Yunus was Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit. He narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, his patron Amr ibn al-As, and Umm Salama. He is described as one of the jurists among the mawali, is said to have seen Abu Bakr, and witnessed the conquest of Egypt. All six collections used him. Ibn Yunus, via Rabi'a al-A'raj from Ibn Lahi'a, states he died in 54 AH.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 2406, pages 5474-5475) gives him as Sufyan ibn Ziyad al-Usfuri, Abu al-Warqa' al-Ahmari (or al-Asadi), of Kufa. He narrated from his father Ziyad, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Shurayh the judge and Ikrima mawla Ibn Abbas; Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama and Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated from him. Yahya ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'a and Abu Hatim graded him thiqa; all six except Muslim used him. Al-Mizzi notes he is distinct from Sufyan al-Tammar. No death year is given on the page.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 829; islamweb vol. 4, p. 374, and shamela.ws/book/3722/1887) gives him as Thabit ibn Qays al-Ghifari (their mawla), Abu al-Ghusn, of Medina. full: Muhammad bin Marwan bin al-Hakam b. Abi al-Aas b. Umayya b. 'Abd Shams b. 'Abd Manaf
teachers: Marwan bin al-Hakam bin Abi al-'As
bio: English Wikipedia states Muhammad ibn Marwan ibn al-Hakam, son of Caliph Marwan I, was an Umayyad prince and leading general of the period 690-710 who completed the Arab conquest of Armenia. He governed North Mesopotamia, Tur Abdin and Harran from 692, and later Mesopotamia, Armenia and Azerbaijan until 709/10. At the Battle of Sebastopolis (692/3) he induced the Slavic contingent of the Byzantine army to defect. His son Marwan II became the last Umayyad caliph. The page gives his death as 719/720 CE (a two-year range) and his kunya as Abu Abd al-Rahman.
research_evidence: Muhammad ibn Marwan ibn al-Hakam (died 719/720) was an Umayyad prince and one of the most important generals of the Umayyad Caliphate

He narrated from his father, Sa'id bin al-Musayyib, Salim bin 'Abdullah bin 'Umar, Sa'd bin Ishaq bin Ka'b bin 'Ujra, 'Ali bin al-Husayn and 'Umar bin 'Abd al-'Aziz; al-Darawardi, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, Ibn Mahdi, Hammad bin Khalid al-Khayyat, Ibn Abi Fudayk and Zayd bin al-Hubab narrated from him. bio: 'Abd al-Hamid bin Mahmud al-Ma'wali, described as Basran (or, according to some, Kufan), is listed in the fourth generation of narrators; the page gives his death only as a range between 111 and 120 AH. bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 1622) records Khalid bin Tahman al-Saluli, Abu al-'Ala' al-Khaffaf of Kufa, also known as Khalid bin Abi Khalid. He narrated from Anas bin Malik, Habib bin Abi Thabit and Husayn bin 'Abd al-Rahman; Sufyan al-Thawri, 'Abdullah bin al-Mubarak, Waki' bin al-Jarrah, Ahmad bin 'Abdullah bin Yunus and Yahya bin 'Abbad narrated from him. Yahya bin Ma'in is reported to have called him weak, while Abu Hatim said he was among the early Shi'a but truthful. Al-Tirmidhi recorded his narrations. No death year is given.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 1627, beginning at /book/3722/3819) records Khalid bin 'Abdullah bin Yazid bin Asad bin Kurz al-Bajali al-Qasri, Abu al-Qasim (also Abu al-Haytham), a Damascene, brother of Asad and Isma'il bin 'Abdullah. He was governor of Mecca under al-Walid and Sulayman bin 'Abd al-Malik and governor of the two Iraqs under Hisham. He narrated from his father from his grandfather; Isma'il bin Abi Khalid, Isma'il bin Awsat, Habib bin Abi Habib al-Jarmi and Humayd al-Tawil narrated from him. Khalifa bin Khayyat says he was killed in 126 AH at about sixty years of age; al-Bukhari puts his killing at Kufa around 120 AH. Al-Bukhari recorded one hadith from him in Af'al al-'Ibad.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 6536, vol. 30 p. 125) gives him as Hashim bin al-Barid, Abu 'Ali al-Kufi, father of 'Ali bin Hashim bin al-Barid. He narrated from Isma'il bin Raja', Isma'il bin Sumay' and al-Asbagh bin Nubata; among those who narrated from him were Abu Qutayba Salm bin Qutayba, Salih bin Abi al-Aswad, 'Abdullah bin Dawud al-Khuraybi and his son 'Ali. Ahmad bin Hanbal (via Abu Talib) said 'la ba's bihi', Yahya bin Ma'in (via Ishaq bin Mansur) said 'thiqa', and Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah recorded his hadith. No death year is given.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 7119) lists Ya'la bin Murra, Abu Murra al-Kufi, distinct from the companion Ya'la bin Murra bin Wahb al-Thaqafi who precedes him. 'Ubayd bin Abi Umayya al-Tanafisi (father of Ya'la bin 'Ubayd) and his brothers narrated from him. Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat, and al-Bukhari recorded this single hadith of his in al-Adab al-Mufrad. No death year is given.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (Kitab al-Kuna) gives Abu al-Rahhal al-Ta'i al-Kufi, whose name is 'Uqba bin 'Ubayd al-Ta'i, brother of Sa'id bin 'Ubayd, as reported by 'Abbas al-Duri from Yahya bin Ma'in. He narrated from Anas bin Malik and Bashir bin Yasar; Hafs bin Ghiyath, his brother Sa'id bin 'Ubayd al-Ta'i, 'Uqba bin Khalid al-Sakuni, 'Isa bin Yunus and Yahya bin Sa'id al-Qattan narrated from him. Al-Bukhari cited him as a supporting witness (istashhada bihi). The page's editorial footnote notes Ibn Hibban criticised his frequent errors and Ibn Hajar graded him 'maqbul'. Distinct from Abu al-Rahhal al-Ansari al-Basri (Muhammad bin Khalid), who precedes him.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (Kitab al-Kuna, entry 7522) describes Abu 'Ukasha al-Hamdani al-Kufi as 'one of the unknowns' (ahad al-majahil). He transmitted from Rifa'a bin Shaddad, from 'Amr bin al-Hamiq, the hadith 'whoever gives a man security for his life and then kills him...', and Abu Layla 'Abdullah bin Maysara al-Harithi narrated it from him; Waki' related it from Abu Layla without naming him, while Muslim bin Ibrahim's version has Rifa'a narrating from Sulayman bin Surad. bio: The shamela.ws narrator index records 'Abdullah bin Rashid al-Zawfi al-Misri al-Himyari al-Madhhiji, kunya Abu al-Dahhak, of the sixth tabaqa. Al-Bukhari noted that his hearing from Ibn Abi Murra could not be verified and that he had only one hadith, on the witr prayer, which al-Tirmidhi called gharib. No death date is given.

His hadith appears in al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Abu Dawud (per the sigla). No death year is given in the entry.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 27, p. 288) lists Mahfuz ibn 'Alqama al-Hadrami, Abu Junada al-Himsi, elder brother of Nasr ibn 'Alqama. He narrated from Salman al-Farisi (said to be mursal), 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'A'idh, his father 'Alqama al-Hadrami, and Yazid ibn Maysara ibn Halbas. Thawr ibn Yazid al-Rahabi, Muhammad ibn Rashid al-Makhuli, his brother Nasr ibn 'Alqama, al-Wadin ibn 'Ata' and others narrated from him. Yahya ibn Ma'in and Duhaym called him thiqa; Abu Zur'a said 'no harm in him'; Ibn Hibban lists him in al-Thiqat. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i (Musnad 'Ali) and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith 'The eye is the string of the anus; when the eye sleeps the string is loosened.' No death year is given.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 27, p. 390, entry 5872) lists Marwan ibn Salim al-Muqaffa'. bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 29, pp. 396-399, entry 6431) lists al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi al-Bahili, their client, Abu Rawh (also said Abu 'Umar or Abu 'Amr), al-Jazari, resident of Harran, who saw the companion Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila. He narrated from Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Ikrima, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Mujahid, Makhul, Maymun ibn Mihran, Nafi' mawla Ibn 'Umar and others; Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama, 'Abda ibn Sulayman, 'Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani, al-Nufayli and many Harranis narrated from him. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Yahya ibn Ma'in, Ibn Numayr, Abu Hatim and al-Nasa'i graded him thiqa or 'no harm in him'; Ibn Sa'd said he was weak and died in the caliphate of al-Mahdi. Abu Ja'far al-Nufayli and Ibn Hibban say he died in 168 AH. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi transmitted his hadith.
research_teachers: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr
research_evidence: وَقَال أَبُو جعفر النفيلي، وابن حبان: مات سنة ثمان وستين. ومئة. روى له أَبُو داود، والتِّرْمِذِيّ. ٦٤٣٢ - بخ: النضر بن علقمة
